# CPI前美債小幅回升，Nvidia釐清融資支持範圍

## 油價再漲，美債仍收復部分跌幅

荷莫茲海峽重啟通航的前景再生變數，油價反彈，美國公債卻在CPI公布前收復部分週一跌幅。2年期殖利率下跌3個基點至4.22%，5年期與10年期各跌2個基點至4.39%及4.70%，30年期跌1個基點至5.24%。短端領漲，殖利率曲線小幅轉陡，2年與10年期利差擴大至48個基點，2年與30年期利差升至102個基點。

10年期名目殖利率的降幅全數來自通膨補償：損益兩平通膨率下跌2個基點至2.27%，實質殖利率維持2.43%。同日WTI上漲1.62%至$83.46，布蘭特原油上漲1.66%至$89.18。債市並未認定供應中斷已經結束，而是在消費者物價公布前，暫不願進一步提高中期通膨定價。

美國內需數據仍有分歧。小企業樂觀程度升至近一年最高，招聘計畫為2022年10月以來最強，對通膨的擔憂則減輕；成屋銷售卻下滑1.7%，年率降至406萬戶、創三個月低點。企業的用人意願比房市表現更有韌性，9月升息機率也仍接近50%，未隨債市反彈明顯消退。

信用市場的發行活動持續，10家投資級發行人合計籌得$166億。ICE與Blue Owl擴大發行規模、收窄定價利差，Nvidia說明基礎設施融資支持的上限後，公司債與CDS利差也隨之收斂。壓力較集中在對能源敏感的新興市場：長天期美元主權債下跌，與長天期美債的漲勢形成對比。

## CPI即將公布，龐大空頭部位可能放大波動

週二漲勢由短端主導，但相較過去一個月長端殖利率的升幅，回落幅度仍小。2年期殖利率近一個月僅升1個基點，5年、10年及30年期分別升9、14及18個基點，2年與30年期利差擴大17個基點。10年期殖利率的月升幅中，實質殖利率貢獻11個基點，損益兩平通膨率貢獻3個基點。

巴基斯坦國防部長Khawaja Asif表示談判正朝和平推進，油價一度下跌；伊朗隨後重申，在其條件獲滿足前，荷莫茲海峽將維持關閉，油價因而反轉。美國能源資訊署（EIA）的預測也顯示，供應衝擊可能持續更久：衝突造成的每日約60萬桶供應損失，可能延續至2027年底。海峽通行量估計已由2025年第4季每日2,160萬桶，降至第2季的490萬桶。

EIA將2026年汽油與柴油價格預測分別上修3.7%及5.4%，2027年零售汽油價格預測也較上月提高6.5%。能源風險因此不只是當日油價的漲跌。不過，損益兩平通膨率仍下滑，顯示投資人希望先從消費者物價看到更廣泛的證據，再提高中期通膨溢價。

NFIB調查顯示，高利率尚未使小企業放棄招募或擴張：樂觀程度與用人計畫同步改善，通膨壓力卻有所減輕。房市受到的融資約束更明顯。成屋銷售降至年率406萬戶、符合預期，高房貸利率與房價繼續壓抑購屋需求。

部位可能讓CPI公布後的反應更加劇烈。瑞銀估計，商品交易顧問（CTA）在7月底將全球債券減碼部位擴大至原來的3倍，10年期殖利率每變動1個基點，相關部位約有$3億損益變化，為其1990年以來資料中的最大曝險。美銀也指出CTA持有大量較短天期公債空單；摩根大通調查則由偏多轉向中性，淨多頭降至5月18日以來最低。這些數據說明市場對意外數據的敏感程度，但不能據此斷定週二漲勢由空頭回補帶動。

現券交易較集中在對政策敏感的天期。名目附息公債成交額增加13.3%至$7,906億，其中超過2年至3年期的成交額倍增至$1,592億；7年至10年期則減少11.0%至$1,398億。成交額反映交易活躍度，本身不區分客戶買賣方向。

長端的買方結構也與十年前不同。隨Fed與外國官方部門需求減弱，民間投資人持有的美債比重估計由約50%升至73%。截至週二，30年期殖利率今年已有41個交易日高於5%，為2007年以來最長紀錄。20年以上美債指數當日上漲0.19%，近一個月仍下跌2.30%。數據公布前的小幅反彈，尚未改變這群更在意價格的投資人對長債報酬的要求。

## 併購融資順利定價，Nvidia界定潛在承擔

信用資產當日報酬不大。LQD上漲0.03%，HYG與JNK各漲約0.04%，長天期AAA–A與BBB指數分別上漲0.04%及0.03%，均落後長天期美債。較值得關注的變化，出現在個別交易的融資條件。

洲際交易所（ICE）發行$37.5億固定利率債券，分為3年至10年的4個年期，協助支付收購MarketAxess的$60億價款。發行額高於當日稍早規劃的約$35億，最長年期利差由初步討論的約115個基點收窄至82個基點，原擬發行的浮動利率部分則取消。這批定期債務將取代最高$62.5億過橋承諾的一部分，確立併購融資來源；後續整合與槓桿負擔仍由公司承擔。

Blue Owl旗下融資子公司的10年期投資級債券，因訂單高峰達約$33億，規模由原先討論的$5億擴大至$7.5億。定價利差收窄約30個基點至220個基點。Blue Owl Capital等12個實體提供保證，資金將償還循環信貸。明確用途與保證架構支持其睽違兩年再度為自身發債籌資，但絕對利差仍高於ICE。

Nvidia則釐清了$5,000億AI基礎設施計畫中的支持範圍。由6家公司組成的聯盟，計畫透過私募及以運算設備作擔保的特殊目的公司（SPV）債券，引入第三方資金。各SPV可能發行數百億美元債務，將設備出租給Nvidia客戶，首批架構可能在數月內推出。這是一個擬議的融資平台，並非Nvidia單獨承擔$5,000億負債。

黃仁勳表示，Nvidia會逐案評估、依資產殘值提供支持，上限為各項投資機會的25%。其2056年到期、票息5.625%的債券利差收窄2個基點至113個基點，5年期CDS最多收窄5個基點至72.11。潛在損失由誰承擔變得較明確，有助信用定價；但Nvidia仍仰賴客戶以融資支應投資，電力、土地、變壓器與晶片的供應瓶頸也非資金到位就能立即解決。

英特爾則展現股票市場的籌資能力。增額後的股票發行籌得$200億，比初始目標多逾三分之一，據報需求超過$1,000億。AI投資風險因此有更廣泛的股本承擔，不必全部轉為公司債或證券化融資。對債權人而言，資金最後能否轉化為可用產能與客戶獲利仍重要，但以何種工具籌資同樣影響信用風險。

Gainwell的資本結構調整仍待完成。公司在$43.4億債券與貸款方案中推出5年期高收益債，截至週二接獲約$40億訂單；加上$14.6億第二順位擔保貸款的條款修改與展延，擬為全部$58億資本結構再融資。穆迪已將其評等由Caa1上調，新債預計落在B級。營收由$4.93億增至$5.26億，調整後EBITDA由$8,700萬增至$9,300萬，但軟體業務受新技術衝擊的風險仍在，交易也須等待本週稍晚執行。

亞特蘭大為哈茲菲爾德－傑克森機場籌發約$10.9億債券，其中約$6.99億適用替代性最低稅（AMT），$3.91億不適用AMT。初步條件顯示，2036年7月到期的AMT債票息為5%、殖利率3.84%，較基準高約60個基點，評等為AA+或AA。機場約$130億現代化計畫還需要$37億債務，預計至2032年再進場3次。2026年機場債供給雖少，這個發行人後續的籌資需求已相當清楚。

## 韓國傾向再升息，澳洲暫待緊縮效果

韓國銀行首席副總裁Ryoo Sangdai表示，強勁成長推升基礎通膨，可能需要進一步升息。7月升息25個基點至2.75%，是2023年初以來首次調升。整體通膨雖降至2.8%，核心卻升至2.6%；第2季經濟成長0.6%、優於預期，按工作日調整的7月出口年增率更接近70%。

8月27日決策將參考更新後的預測、高頻支出數據與金融穩定情勢。韓元近期雖回升，整體仍偏弱、增加進口成本；半導體景氣則支持薪資與消費。央行面對的是內需強度是否讓通膨更久高於目標，而不只是油價單日上漲。韓國利率若續升，也會提高本地資產相對美元債券的吸引力。

澳洲連續第二次將利率維持在4.35%，等待失業率上升與房市轉弱進一步冷卻需求。不過，總裁布洛克仍稱再次緊縮的可能性相當高。通膨偏離2%至3%目標區間中點已有約五年，使央行難以對提早降息建立信心。英國零售銷售金額年增率則僅1.3%，為前一年增速的一半，呈現另一個需求放緩訊號。

歐洲物流面對的卻是供給問題。萊茵河考布水位降至1880年有紀錄以來最低，部分航運業者稱河道已無法通行，可能需要數週降雨才有改善。工業核心地帶的運輸限制，加上更東側地區乾旱對電力與農業的壓力，使消費轉弱原本可能帶來的通膨降溫效果打了折扣。

## 菲律賓擴大借款，能源成本牽動各國政策

美元指數維持99.81，新興市場匯率與股票指數卻各跌0.1%；油價上漲之際，印度及東歐本地殖利率也走高。長天期新興市場美元主權債指數下跌0.25%，相較之下長天期美債上漲0.19%，EMB則微跌0.01%。當日壓力主要來自能源曝險與各國財政，而非美元普遍走強。

菲律賓提出2027年借款₱3.3兆、約$540億的計畫，比2026年修正後的₱2.73兆增加20%。借款將支應₱7.2兆預算的46%，赤字目標由GDP的4.8%擴大至5.1%。6月債務已達₱19.07兆、約GDP的66%。這個逾90%石油來自中東的經濟體，正以財政支出因應成長疲弱與能源紓困需求。

本地借款預計增加24%至₱2.39兆，占總額約72%；國際債券發行規劃由₱3,144億增至₱3,660億，2026年至今已在全球市場籌得$52.5億。提高本地融資比重可減少即時外幣需求，卻也增加國內投資人必須吸收的供給。今年本地債以匯率避險後美元計價已跌5%，披索下跌3.7%，財政支持面臨融資成本上升的牽制。

肯亞連續第三次維持利率8.75%，符合全部5份預測，重點在穩定預期與匯率。燃料成本傳導至食品與運輸，使整體通膨由6.4%升至6.5%，核心由3.1%升至3.2%。央行認為通膨可留在2.5%至7.5%區間，前提是衝突降溫；農作歉收與可能出現的超級聖嬰現象另添食品風險，不能將暫停調整解讀為即將降息。

巴西7月CPI年增率降至4.44%，略高於預期中值4.4%，月增0.07%。食品飲料下跌0.67%、服飾下跌0.66%，住宅相關價格則上漲0.99%。8月5日會議紀錄強調，通膨預期偏離目標，仍須讓政策較長時間維持緊縮；當次雖連續第四度降息25個基點至14%，累計降幅達100個基點，2028年底通膨預期3.8%仍高於3%目標。實際物價降溫容許央行逐步調降利率，但不足以解除政策約束。

哥倫比亞則突然面臨重建支出。規模7.4地震造成至少130人死亡、咖啡產區受損，新任總統Abelardo de la Espriella才剛帶著削減40%公共支出的承諾上任。政府計畫宣布經濟緊急狀態，藉此不經國會核准發布臨時稅務及經濟命令。救災需要彈性，資金安排仍將檢驗新政府的財政整頓承諾與非常權力的運用。

## 油金同漲，尚未出現全面去槓桿

談判尚未帶來實際通航，WTI與布蘭特原油分別上漲1.62%及1.66%，黃金期貨也漲1.52%至$4,428.20，美元則持平。商品市場的避險需求，與美債損益兩平通膨率下降同時出現：迫切的地緣風險仍在，但CPI公布前，投資人並未同步提高中期通膨補償。

S&P 500與Nasdaq 100各跌約0.32%，半導體指數則在AI融資及營運消息下上漲0.87%。VIX下跌1.16%至15.28，配合信用發行順利、股市跌幅溫和，未見流動性全面撤出的跡象。長天期新興主權債落後長天期美債，也與個別國家較高的能源及財政敏感度一致。

## CPI將考驗空頭部位，長債標售接續登場

週三公布7月CPI，市場預期整體物價月增0.1%，前值為月減0.4%。其中一份預測估計能源將拖累11個基點，核心年增率可能降至2021年3月以來最低。若數據溫和、服務價格漲勢也不廣泛，短端行情可能延續，迫使龐大的CTA空頭調整；若多個項目普遍高於預期，當日損益兩平通膨率下跌2個基點的定價便可能逆轉，油價之外的內生通膨將重新受到關注。隨後的生產者物價可再補充上游成本線索。

荷莫茲海峽仍須看到持續通行、各方接受條件，以及運費與保險障礙下降。若運輸改善，且油價降至週二WTI $83.46、布蘭特$89.18以下，EIA上修後的燃料價格路徑便有下調空間。反之，持續關閉或通行量仍遠低於戰前每日2,160萬桶，即使7月CPI受惠於較早的能源跌價，供給問題也未消失。韓國、肯亞與菲律賓則可分別觀察這股壓力如何進入國內物價與政策。

週四$250億30年期美債標售，將在殖利率約5.24%、今年已有41個交易日高於5%的背景下測試需求。民間買方比重提高後，投資人配售、標售讓利與後續交易，比殖利率水準本身更能說明承接力。Gainwell預計本週稍晚完成的債券與貸款交易，則提供企業融資的對照：若無須增加讓利便能完成，表示原擬架構可獲市場接受；若訂單轉弱或條件改變，槓桿融資的價格敏感度就仍待消化。

overall_summary.headline: CPI前美債小幅回升，Nvidia釐清融資支持範圍
overall_summary.session_narrative:
美債收復部分週一跌幅，10年期殖利率下跌2個基點至4.70%，降幅全數來自損益兩平通膨率，實質殖利率維持2.43%。伊朗重申荷莫茲海峽重啟條件，WTI與布蘭特原油再度上漲。

小企業招聘計畫增強，成屋銷售卻下滑，9月升息機率仍接近50%。瑞銀估計，10年期殖利率每變動1個基點，CTA債券部位約有$3億損益變化，使CPI成為重要的部位考驗。

10家投資級發行人合計籌得$166億。ICE與Blue Owl增額發行、收窄定價，Nvidia說明逐案支持的上限後，債券與CDS利差也收斂。相較之下，菲律賓擴大借款與能源敏感的新興市場，更能看到融資壓力。

long_thesis.english_markdown:
# Bonds edge higher before CPI as Nvidia defines its financing exposure

## Treasuries resist another oil advance

Treasuries recovered some of Monday's losses before CPI, even as renewed doubts over Hormuz pushed oil higher again. The two-year yield fell 3 basis points to 4.22%, five- and ten-year yields declined 2 to 4.39% and 4.70%, and the 30-year eased 1 to 5.24%. The front end led a modest steepening, taking 2s10s to 48 basis points and 2s30s to 102.

At ten years, the entire nominal decline came from inflation compensation: the breakeven fell 2 basis points to 2.27% while the real yield stayed at 2.43%. WTI nevertheless rose 1.62% to $83.46 and Brent gained 1.66% to $89.18. Investors were not declaring the physical disruption over; they were reluctant to add more medium-term inflation compensation immediately before the consumer-price report.

Domestic data offered no single answer on restraint. Small-business optimism reached its highest in almost a year and hiring plans their strongest since October 2022, while inflation concerns eased. Existing-home sales fell 1.7% to a 4.06 million annualized rate, a three-month low. Business intentions were firmer than the housing market, and September hike odds remained near 50% despite the bond rally.

Primary credit stayed active, with ten investment-grade issuers raising $16.6 billion. ICE and Blue Owl enlarged transactions and tightened pricing, while Nvidia's explanation of limits on its infrastructure-financing support narrowed its bond and CDS spreads. The pressure was more apparent in oil-sensitive emerging markets, where long dollar sovereign bonds fell even as long Treasuries gained.

## Heavy short positions meet an uncertain inflation release

Tuesday's rally was strongest at the front end but small compared with the accumulated rise in long yields. Over a month, the two-year was up only 1 basis point, the five-year 9, the ten-year 14 and the 30-year 18. The 2s30s curve had steepened 17 basis points. At ten years, 11 basis points of the monthly rise came through real yields and 3 through breakevens.

Oil initially declined after Pakistani Defense Minister Khawaja Asif said talks were moving toward peace. Prices reversed when Iran reiterated that Hormuz would remain closed until its conditions were met. The EIA added a longer horizon to the disruption, projecting about 600,000 barrels a day of conflict-related supply losses through end-2027. Estimated Hormuz flows had fallen from 21.6 million barrels a day in the fourth quarter of 2025 to 4.9 million in the second quarter.

The agency raised its 2026 gasoline and diesel price forecasts by 3.7% and 5.4%, and its 2027 retail-gasoline estimate by 6.5% from the previous month's projection. Those revisions keep energy relevant beyond the next settlement price. The decline in breakevens nevertheless showed that investors were waiting for broader evidence in consumer prices before assigning a larger medium-term inflation premium.

The NFIB survey suggested smaller firms had not abandoned hiring or expansion in response to high rates. Stronger plans and optimism came alongside easing inflation pressure. Home closings, by contrast, fell to 4.06 million annualized, in line with expectations, as elevated mortgage rates and prices constrained demand. Housing was showing the effects of expensive financing more clearly than business intentions.

Positioning could amplify the response to CPI. UBS estimated commodity trading advisers had tripled their global bond underweight at end-July and now stood to gain or lose about $300 million for each basis-point move in ten-year yields, the largest exposure in its series since 1990. Bank of America also identified substantial CTA shorts in shorter notes. JPMorgan's survey shifted from long toward neutral, with its net-long reading the smallest since May 18. These measures identify sensitivity to a surprise, not proof that Tuesday's gains were short covering.

Cash activity was concentrated closer to the policy-sensitive sector. Nominal-coupon turnover rose 13.3% to $790.6 billion. Activity above two years and through three years more than doubled to $159.2 billion, while seven- to ten-year turnover fell 11.0% to $139.8 billion. Those are gross trading measures; they do not identify the direction of customer demand.

The long end faces a different marginal buyer than it did a decade ago. Private investors hold an estimated 73% of Treasuries, up from roughly 50%, as Fed and foreign-official demand has receded. Through Tuesday, the 30-year yield had spent 41 trading days above 5% this year, the longest such run since 2007. The Treasury index beyond 20 years gained 0.19% on the day but remained down 2.30% over a month. A small pre-data rally did not remove the higher return demanded by more price-sensitive holders.

## Acquisitions clear, and Nvidia limits its potential obligation

Credit returns were modest. LQD gained 0.03%, HYG and JNK about 0.04% each, and long AAA–A and BBB indexes 0.04% and 0.03%, less than long Treasuries. The more consequential developments were in individual financing terms.

Intercontinental Exchange sold $3.75 billion across four fixed-rate tranches from three to ten years to help fund the $6 billion MarketAxess acquisition. The sale grew from about $3.5 billion sought earlier in the day. Its longest tranche priced 82 basis points over Treasuries, down from initial discussion near 115, while a floating-rate tranche was dropped. The fixed-rate deal replaces part of a bridge commitment of up to $6.25 billion, turning acquisition funding into term debt without removing the integration and leverage obligations.

Blue Owl's finance subsidiary increased a ten-year high-grade note from an initially discussed $500 million to $750 million after peak orders reached about $3.3 billion. Pricing tightened roughly 30 basis points to 220 over Treasuries. Twelve entities, including Blue Owl Capital, guarantee the debt, whose proceeds will repay revolver borrowings. Guarantor support and a defined balance-sheet use helped its return to its own bond market after two years, albeit at a wider absolute spread than ICE.

Nvidia reduced uncertainty by describing the boundary of its support for the $500 billion AI-infrastructure initiative. The six-firm coalition intends to mobilize third-party capital through private offerings and special-purpose-vehicle bonds secured by compute. Vehicles could each issue tens of billions of dollars and lease equipment to Nvidia customers, with initial structures potentially coming within months. It is a prospective financing platform, not a single $500 billion Nvidia liability.

Jensen Huang said Nvidia's support would be capped at up to 25% of an opportunity, assessed project by project and linked to residual value. Its 5.625% bond due in 2056 tightened 2 basis points to 113 over Treasuries; five-year CDS tightened as much as 5 basis points to 72.11. Clarifying who would bear losses helped the credit. It did not eliminate dependence on financed customer spending or shortages of power, land, transformers and chips that additional capital cannot immediately solve.

Intel showed the scale available through equity instead. An upsized share sale raised $20 billion, more than a third above its initial target, with reported demand exceeding $100 billion. That broadens the pool bearing AI investment risk rather than sending every funding requirement into bonds or securitizations. The money still has to become usable capacity and customer earnings, but its form matters to creditors assessing the buildout.

Gainwell's proposed overhaul remained more conditional. It launched a five-year high-yield bond within a $4.34 billion bond-and-loan package, with approximately $4 billion of orders by Tuesday. Alongside amendment and extension of a $1.46 billion second-lien loan, the transactions would refinance its full $5.8 billion capital structure. Moody's had upgraded it from Caa1, and the bond was expected in single-B territory. Revenue rose from $493 million to $526 million and adjusted EBITDA from $87 million to $93 million, while software-disruption risk and execution later in the week remained relevant.

Atlanta brought about $1.09 billion for Hartsfield-Jackson airport, split between roughly $699 million of alternative-minimum-tax bonds and $391 million of non-AMT debt. Preliminary terms for July 2036 AMT bonds showed a 5% coupon and 3.84% yield, about 60 basis points over the benchmark, with ratings of AA+ or AA. The airport's roughly $13 billion modernization plan requires another $3.7 billion of debt and three expected market visits through 2032. Scarce airport supply in 2026 therefore comes with a visible recurring borrower calendar.

## Korea leans toward more restraint; Australia waits

Bank of Korea Senior Deputy Governor Ryoo Sangdai said further increases would probably be needed as strong growth feeds underlying inflation. July's 25-basis-point rise to 2.75% was the first since early 2023. Headline inflation had cooled to 2.8%, but core edged up to 2.6%, second-quarter growth reached a stronger-than-expected 0.6%, and working-day-adjusted July exports rose almost 70% from a year earlier.

The August 27 decision will depend on revised forecasts, high-frequency spending and financial stability. A generally weak won still raises import costs despite its recent recovery, while the semiconductor boom supports wages and consumption. The issue is whether domestic strength prolongs above-target inflation, not simply whether oil rises for another day. Higher Korean rates would also increase the attraction of local assets relative to dollar bonds.

Australia held at 4.35% for a second meeting, relying on higher unemployment and a weaker property market to cool activity. Governor Michele Bullock still said further tightening was quite possible. The bank has missed the midpoint of its 2%–3% target for about five years, limiting confidence in an early easing path. British retail-sales value grew only 1.3% from a year earlier, half the preceding year's pace, adding a separate indication of softer demand.

European logistics faced a supply problem rather than a demand signal. Rhine water at Kaub fell to its lowest level in records dating to 1880, and some shippers described the route as already impassable. Relief could require weeks of rain. Transport constraints in the industrial core joined drought pressure on power and agriculture further east, complicating the benefit weaker spending might otherwise offer to inflation and bonds.

## Philippine borrowing expands as oil strains local policy

The Dollar Index was unchanged at 99.81, but developing-market currency and equity gauges each fell 0.1% as oil rose and local yields increased in India and eastern Europe. The long EM dollar sovereign index lost 0.25%, against a 0.19% gain in long Treasuries; EMB was nearly flat at −0.01%. Energy exposure and local fiscal risks mattered more than a common dollar squeeze.

The Philippines proposed PHP3.3 trillion, or $54 billion, of borrowing in 2027, up 20% from this year's revised PHP2.73 trillion. Borrowing would finance 46% of a PHP7.2 trillion budget, with the deficit target widening from 4.8% to 5.1% of GDP. Debt stood at PHP19.07 trillion, about 66% of GDP, in June. The plan follows weak growth and energy-relief measures in an economy sourcing more than 90% of its oil from the Middle East.

Local borrowing would rise 24% to PHP2.39 trillion, about 72% of the total. International bond issuance is planned at PHP366 billion, up from PHP314.4 billion, after $5.25 billion raised globally in 2026. Domestic reliance limits immediate foreign-currency needs but increases the supply local investors must absorb. Local bonds have lost 5% in hedged-dollar terms this year and the peso is down 3.7%, leaving fiscal support to compete with higher financing costs.

Kenya held at 8.75% for a third meeting, matching all five forecasts, to stabilize expectations and the exchange rate. Inflation rose from 6.4% to 6.5% and core from 3.1% to 3.2%, as fuel passed into food and transport. The central bank's expectation that inflation stays within its 2.5%–7.5% band assumes de-escalation. Crop failure and a possible super El Nino add food risks, so the hold is conditional stability rather than a signal of imminent easing.

Brazil's July CPI slowed to 4.44%, slightly above the 4.4% median, with a monthly increase of 0.07%. Food and beverages fell 0.67% and clothing 0.66%, while housing rose 0.99%. Minutes of the August 5 decision emphasized that deanchored expectations require tighter policy for longer, despite the fourth consecutive quarter-point cut to 14% and 100 basis points of cumulative easing. End-2028 expectations of 3.8% remain above the 3% target. Realized disinflation was permitting gradual reductions, not removing the need for restraint.

Colombia faced an unplanned reconstruction burden. A magnitude-7.4 earthquake killed at least 130 people and damaged the coffee region just as President Abelardo de la Espriella took office promising a 40% reduction in public outlays. The government planned an economic-emergency declaration allowing temporary tax and economic decrees without congressional approval. Disaster relief can justify flexibility, but its funding will test the new administration's consolidation promise and use of extraordinary powers.

## Oil and gold rise without broad deleveraging

WTI gained 1.62% and Brent 1.66% as negotiations failed to produce physical reopening, while gold futures rose 1.52% to $4,428.20. The dollar was flat. The protection bid in commodities coexisted with lower Treasury breakevens, separating acute geopolitical risk from the medium-term inflation compensation investors were willing to pay before CPI.

The S&P 500 and Nasdaq 100 each fell about 0.32%, but semiconductors rose 0.87% amid AI financing and operating news. VIX declined 1.16% to 15.28. Credit execution and modest equity moves did not suggest a general withdrawal of liquidity. Long EM sovereign debt was weaker than long Treasuries, consistent with the greater energy and fiscal sensitivities visible in individual markets.

## CPI confronts a heavily positioned market

Wednesday's July CPI forecast calls for a 0.1% headline increase after a 0.4% decline. One projection assigns an 11-basis-point drag from energy and puts core annual inflation at its lowest since March 2021. A benign report with limited service-price breadth could support the front-end rally and force adjustments in the large CTA short positions. A broad upside surprise would challenge the 2-basis-point breakeven decline and bring domestic persistence back alongside the oil shock. Producer prices follow with another view of pipeline costs.

Hormuz still needs sustained passage, accepted terms and lower freight and insurance friction. Improvement alongside oil below Tuesday's $83.46 WTI and $89.18 Brent closes would weaken the EIA's higher fuel-price path. Continued closure or traffic far below the prewar 21.6 million-barrel daily pace would keep the supply problem active even if July CPI benefited from earlier energy declines. Korea, Kenya and the Philippines offer different tests of how far that pressure is reaching domestic prices and policy.

Thursday's $25 billion 30-year sale will test demand near a 5.24% yield after 41 sessions above 5%. Investor allocations, any concession and subsequent trading matter more than the level alone in a market increasingly held by private buyers. Gainwell's expected bond-and-loan execution later in the week provides a corporate comparison: completing the planned refinancing without larger concessions would show capacity on the proposed structure; weaker orders or changed terms would reveal further price sensitivity in leveraged finance.
